comment: Known answers for OWASP NodeGoat. Every defect below is taken from NodeGoat's own tutorial pages (app/views/tutorial/a1..a10, ssrf) and then confirmed against the source line. We did not plant any of them and did not choose them to suit our rules, which is the point: the code is external, so a perfect score here means something a perfect score on mock/ cannot.
authored_by: ai-sec, from the target's own documentation

defects.cause: req.body values are passed to eval(), so a request executes JavaScript on the server
defects.source: tutorial a1 — 'routes/contributions.js ... makes application vulnerable to SSJS attack'

defects.cause: needle.get() is called with a URL built from req.query.url, so the server fetches whatever the caller names
not_the_cause: an open redirect — the server makes the request, not the browser

defects.cause: the user id is taken from the URL and used to fetch allocations with no check that it belongs to the caller
not_the_cause: injection — the value is used as a parameter, not concatenated
defects.source: tutorial a4 — 'routes/allocations.js, the insecure application takes user id from url'

defects.cause: the benefits routes carry isLoggedIn but no role check, so any authenticated non-admin user reaches an admin-only module by visiting the URL
not_the_cause: missing authentication - isLoggedIn is present on these routes
the link being hidden in the UI for non-admins
defects.source: tutorial a7 — 'there is no authorization check for benefits related routes in routes/index.js'
defects.teaches: authenticated is not authorized; a guard that answers who you are does not answer what you may do

defects.cause: the template engine is configured with autoescape:false, so every value rendered anywhere in the application is rendered as markup
not_the_cause: the profile handler failing to escape - it does call an encoder
reflected XSS - the payload is persisted first
defects.source: tutorial a3 - In server.js, enable the HTML Encoding using template engine auto escape flag
defects.teaches: one line of configuration can be the cause of a vulnerability in every view; reviewing handlers one at a time never finds it

defects.cause: a redirect target is taken from the request without an allowlist
not_the_cause: SSRF — the browser follows it, the server does not

defects.cause: SSN and date of birth are written to the database in cleartext; the file's own comment says they should be encrypted
not_the_cause: weak transport — this is data at rest

defects.cause: the lockfile pins versions with published advisories
not_the_cause: any single package — the finding is the set
defects.cwe_note: trivy files each CVE under that CVE own weakness, so a single CWE cannot key this class

defects.cause: the bank routing number is validated with /([0-9]+)+#/, a quantified group that is itself quantified
not_the_cause: missing input validation - validation is present and is itself the defect
defects.teaches: a control can be the vulnerability
defects.source: tutorial redos - the regexPattern is insecure and vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking
